item.title: Enhancing Spatiotemporal InSAR Retrieval of Snow Water Equivalent Using Multichannel and MAP Estimators
item.description: Differential repeat-pass interferometric synthetic aperture radar (d-InSAR) is an emerging method for retrieving seasonal snow water equivalent (SWE). The technique presents several limitations and sources of uncertainty related to decorrelation and phase ambiguities. For this reason, low-frequency bands are commonly preferred as they offer greater unambiguous retrieval ranges and coherence conservation. However, they lack sensitivity to small changes in snow mass due to long wavelengths. High-frequency bands provide higher sensitivity but suffer from decorrelation and phase wrapping under heavy snow accumulation. Future SAR satellite missions may enable simultaneous acquisitions. MultiChannel (MCh) techniques leverage the combination of statistically independent measurements to reduce noise and ambiguities. This study formulates MCh techniques for retrieving changes in SWE ( $\Delta \mathrm {SWE}$ ) using d-InSAR. Three MCh configurations were evaluated: L- and S-, L- and C-, and C- and X-bands. The theoretical performance was analyzed using the Cramér–Rao lower bound (CRLB). Experimental validation employed SodSAR, a 1–10 GHz tower-based SAR system, and compared single-band and MCh retrievals of $\Delta \mathrm {SWE}$ against in situ snow scale measurements. Additionally, semisynthetic simulations based on ALOS-2 data and a numerical snow model are provided for assessing distributed retrievals employing spatial filtering and Maximum a Posteriori (MAP) estimates. Results demonstrate that MCh configurations have the potential to improve retrieval accuracy, reduce noise, and resolve phase ambiguities.
item.authors: Jorge Jorge-Ruiz;Manu Holmberg;Juha Lemmetyinen;Ioanna Merkouriadi;Anna Kontu;Jouni Pulliainen;Jaan Praks;

item.title: The Neuro-Physical Inverter: A Modular Framework for Magnetotelluric Inversion Coupling Ensemble Conditioning With Residual Learning
item.description: We present the neuro-physical inverter (NPI), a modular, uncertainty-aware framework for geophysical inversion that couples ensemble-based conditioning with constrained residual learning, demonstrated in the 1-D magnetotelluric (MT) setting as a controlled testbed. The framework operates in two stages. An Ensemble-Conditional Gaussian Process (EnsCGP) conditions a prior ensemble of resistivity models on the observed response, producing a physically admissible reference ensemble. A residual-learning neural network then predicts targeted corrections to this reference, trained on synthetic data and fine-tuned per station for field application through a physics-coupled objective. Because an ensemble is conditioned, refined, and propagated through both stages, every estimate carries an associated ensemble spread. Synthetic experiments show that NPI systematically reduces ensemble-mean error without destabilizing the ensemble. Applied to broadband MT data from the Gabbs Valley geothermal region (Nevada, USA), NPI reduces the across-station mean misfit over the mid-period band while retaining comparable ensemble spread. The propagated ensemble yields a factor of uncertainty that serves as an operational measure of constraint within the assumed model class. Both stages are dimension-agnostic in formulation, and the design principles established here are intended to scale to higher-dimensional parameterizations.
item.authors: Jae Deok Kim;Sai Ravela;Rob. L. Evans;

item.title: Doppler Frequency Shift Estimation Based on the First Three Moments for River Surface Velocity Measurement Using Coherent S-Band Doppler Radar
item.description: Microwave Doppler radar enables noncontact and real-time measurements of river surface velocity. However, wind direction modulation causes asymmetric energy distribution of the Doppler spectrum, which shifts the centroid frequency away from the Doppler frequency shift corresponding to radial surface velocity and further introduces significant measurement biases in river surface velocity. To address this issue, this article proposes a Doppler frequency shift correction method based on the first three moments. First, an empirical S-band radar river Doppler model, physically motivated by Bragg scattering and beamwidth-induced Doppler broadening, is established. This model reveals the asymmetry of spectral energy distribution induced by wind direction modulation and characterizes the Doppler broadening mainly caused by the spatial variation of radial surface velocity within the illuminated area. Second, considering the relationship between the effective spectral width of the first-order Bragg peak and the frequency shift under a locally uniform flow field condition, two candidate frequency shifts are derived by combining the centroid frequency and the second moment. Finally, the frequency shift correction is determined according to the sign of the third moment. The simulation results verify that the proposed method can eliminate frequency shift estimation bias by utilizing the statistical characteristics of the Doppler spectrum. Field experiments were carried out in the Xiantao section of the Hanjiang River from May to August 2024. The experimental results show that the root-mean-square error (RMSE) of the surface velocity obtained by the proposed method is less than 0.1 m/s, with a correlation coefficient (CC) higher than 0.9. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can improve the measurement accuracy of river surface velocity for coherent S-band radar.
item.authors: Zheyuan He;Zezong Chen;Fan Ding;Chen Zhao;

item.title: BoxCLIP: Vision–Language Joint Learning for Box-Supervised Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: Weakly supervised change detection (WSCD) aims to reduce annotation costs by replacing dense pixel-level labels with coarse-grained supervision. Within the WSCD paradigm, box-supervised change detection (CD) leverages bounding boxes to annotate change regions. However, existing box-supervised methods often struggle with inaccurate localization of subtle changes and blurred boundaries. To address these challenges, we propose BoxCLIP, a vision–language joint learning framework for box-supervised remote sensing CD (RSCD). The framework first generates image-specific land-cover semantic descriptions with large language models (LLMs), and fuses them with bitemporal visual features through a vision–language joint learning stage, thereby enhancing the semantic discriminability of change-aware representations. Guided by these LLM-derived semantic priors, the proposed method further applies level-set evolution under box-level supervision together with a joint self-supervised strategy, refining the coarse box annotations into precise physical contours and thereby alleviating boundary blurring while recovering fine-grained change instances. Extensive experiments on three public benchmark datasets, WHU-CD, CD-DATA-GZ, and LEVIR-CD, demonstrate that BoxCLIP achieves excellent performance under box-level supervision, attaining $F1$ -scores of 92.16%, 85.02%, and 88.83%, respectively, while substantially reducing annotation costs and maintaining competitive efficiency. The code is available at https://github.com/TiffenYi/BoxCLIP
item.authors: Tingfeng Yi;Fang Liu;Kanghua Yin;Yan Huang;Jia Liu;Xu Tang;Liang Xiao;

item.title: Edge-Guided Adjacent Scale Fusion Network for Building Change Detection With VHR Remote Sensing Images
item.description: Building change detection (BCD) with very high-resolution (VHR) remotely sensed images (RSIs) is crucial in various remote sensing applications. However, most existing multiscale methods mainly aggregate features from different levels, while the relationships and discriminative differences between adjacent-scale features are seldom explicitly modeled. Existing edge-guided methods generally use building boundaries only as auxiliary constraints, without explicitly exploiting building-edge differences between bitemporal images. In this work, motivated by the idea of utilizing multiscale feature difference, a novel encoder–decoder network called edge-guided adjacent-scale fusion (EGASF) network is proposed for BCD with VHR RSIs. First, taking into account the connection of a target between different scales, an adjacent-scale feature fusion (ASFF) module is constructed to join the features from different scales. Second, a multiscale feature difference metric (MFDM) module is proposed to measure the change magnitude between the learned features of different scales. Finally, a building-edge difference extraction (BEDE) module is proposed and coupled with the learned multiscale difference feature to guide the decoding progress for the task of BCD, complementing the loss of information at the stage of the encoder. Experiments on four pairs of real BCD datasets effectively verified the superiority of the proposed EGASF network compared with eight state-of-the-art methods. Compared with the best-performing competing method on each dataset, the proposed EGASF achieves absolute OA improvements of 0.30, 0.82, and 0.52 percentage points on Data-A, Data-B, and Data-C, respectively, while obtaining a comparable result on Data-D. The code for the proposed EGASF network can be available at https://github.com/ImgSciGroup/EGASF-Net
item.authors: Linfu Xie;Zhiyong Lv;Cheng Shi;Jón Atli Benediktsson;Ziqing Zhao;Lubin Tian;

item.title: Full-Waveform Inversion Using Progressive Geological Guidance and Learned Waveform Matching
item.description: The full-waveform inversion (FWI) is highly sensitive to cycle skipping, local minima, and nonuniqueness, particularly when the starting model is smooth and seismic observations provide limited constraints on the subsurface velocity. As a result, waveform matching alone may lead to models that are kinematically acceptable but geologically unreliable. In this study, we propose progressive geology-guided neural (PGGNeural) FWI framework that combines a Siamese representation-based data misfit with sparse well calibration and dip-guided structural regularization. The learned misfit compares observed and simulated shot gathers in a feature space, while the well and dip constraints provide local velocity control and structural guidance during model updating. The proposed framework progressively updates the structural dip guidance as the velocity model evolves, with a weaker dip contribution in the first step and stronger guidance in subsequent steps to stabilize the inversion. Experiments on the British Petroleum (BP) salt and Marmousi models show that PGGNeural produces more accurate and geologically coherent velocity models than benchmarks, with reduced coherent data residuals and improved reverse time migration (RTM) imaging responses. The analyses of progressive updating and well control settings further illustrate how geological guidance improves the stability of the inversion pathway and the recovery of complex salt and layered structures. The proposed framework provides a practical way to improve the convergence behavior and geological reliability of neural FWI by combining learned waveform matching with progressive geological constraints.
item.authors: Liuqing Yang;Min Bai;Dong Zhang;Zixiang Zhou;Xufa Zheng;Hang Xu;Yatong Zhou;

item.title: Bayes-Risk Theory of Task-Posterior Diffusion for Sparse Multimodal Remote Sensing Detection
item.description: This article studies a formal Bayes-risk version of the open problem identified by Liu et al. (2024) (TGRS): task specific, end-to-end, and multimodal remote sensing diffusion for interpretation tasks. Existing diffusion pipelines often learn an image distribution or image score and attach a detector afterward, but this separation is not well matched to small sparse object detection, where target evidence can be weak in the main image, distributed across auxiliary modalities, or hidden by foreground–background imbalance. We study a decision-calibrated task-posterior diffusion formulation for this setting. Detection is modeled on a finite set of valid anchors, and a class-balanced risk is used to avoid the trivial all-background solution. Under a local Gaussian model with whitened image anchors and auxiliary modal features, the image-only and multimodal risks have closed forms. The image-only risk depends on diffused image contrast, while the multimodal task-posterior risk also contains an auxiliary Mahalanobis information term. Any nonzero whitened auxiliary contrast gives a strict Bayes-risk improvement. When the main-image contrast vanishes, the image-only detector tends to random guessing, while the multimodal detector remains nondegenerate if auxiliary information persists. We also prove population consistency, characterize the decision-calibrated posterior score, and give stability margins for posterior error and total-variation deviations. Without Gaussianity or conditional independence, a distribution-free total-variation result still guarantees that adding modalities cannot increase the optimal balanced risk. On real VEDAI RGB–NIR anchors, a decision-score Gaussian Q–Q $R^{2}$ of 0.929 and full-covariance closed-form/held-out errors of $0.062/0.070$ support the approximation’s decision-level utility; RGB alone gives $0.092/0.093$ .
item.authors: Wentao Zhang;Wentao Mo;

item.title: Bilateral Filtering-Guided Adaptive Anisotropic Total Variation Seismic Impedance Inversion
item.description: Seismic impedance inversion is a fundamental technique for deriving impedance from seismic data, providing essential information for reservoir characterization. Existing inversion methods can impose lateral constraints to suppress noise and enhance the lateral continuity of inversion results. However, such lateral constraints tend to impair the edge information of complex discontinuous structures while suppressing the noise. As a result, it is difficult to effectively preserve stratigraphic boundaries with these constraints. To address these limitations, this article proposes a bilateral filtering-guided adaptive anisotropic total variation (ATV) regularization method for impedance inversion. Different from the conventional approach that serially concatenates inversion and filtering, the key innovation is the construction of an adaptive weight matrix that directly integrates the filtering process into the formulation of the inversion objective function. Consequently, the inversion process is inherently guided by the filtering information, dynamically adjusting the lateral and vertical constraint strengths to suppress noise in flat regions while preserving stratigraphic discontinuities at boundaries. The split Bregman algorithm combined with the 2-D-Sylvester equation is employed to solve the inversion objective function by decomposing the complex multiparameter optimization problem into tractable subproblems. Experimental results on synthetic models and field data demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in inversion accuracy compared with conventional approaches, and effectively balances noise suppression with edge preservation.
item.authors: Ziwen Liu;Xuehua Chen;Qingwei Zhao;Wei Jiang;Shengyi Wang;

item.title: Time–Frequency-Guided Audio–Visual Distillation for Lightweight Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition
item.description: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) relies on both temporal waveforms and spectral representations, which provide complementary cues for classification. However, existing knowledge distillation (KD) approaches in UATR predominantly adopt a single-modality paradigm, which transfers knowledge either from audio waveforms or spectrograms alone. This neglect of cross-domain complementarity limits their effectiveness. To overcome these challenges, we propose time–frequency-guided audio–visual distillation (TFAVD), a dual-teacher framework that integrates temporal and spectral knowledge into a lightweight student model. Specifically, the global-aware audio distillation (GAD) module transfers multilevel temporal dynamics from a wav2vec 2.0 audio teacher, while the cross-modal visual distillation (CVD) module captures complementary spectral patterns from Mel and constant-Q transform (CQT) representations. To bridge the modality gap between temporal and spectral domains, we introduce a cross-self-supervised alignment paradigm that unifies their feature spaces and enables efficient knowledge fusion. Experimental results on three real-world oceanic datasets show that TFAVD achieves a promising accuracy of 92.39% ( $\uparrow ~1.47$ % versus 90.92%), demonstrating its capability to enable resource-efficient UATR systems.
item.authors: Hanlin Cui;Zongzheng Wu;Xiaohui Chu;Bingbing Qi;Runze Hu;Shefeng Yan;

item.title: Dual-Noise-Augmented Consistency Learning for Semi-Supervised Building Change Detection
item.description: Building change detection (BCD) using remotely sensed images is critical for urban monitoring and disaster response. However, fully supervised methods suffer from high labeling costs, imbalanced change types, and noise interference. Although existing semi-supervised methods can reduce labeling cost by jointly learning with limited labeled data and abundant unlabeled data, they tend to introduce distribution bias when generating pseudo-samples and are prone to overfitting under imbalanced change types. To address these issues, we propose a semi-supervised change detection framework using dual-noise augmentation consistency learning (DACL-CD), aiming at improving hybrid sample generation and leveraging unlabeled data more effectively. First, we introduce a dual-noise augmentation CutMix learning (DNACL) to generate hybrid samples while reducing distortion in pseudo-samples. We further propose a progressive teacher–student consistent learning framework, focusing on dual-temporal feature representation and consistency learning, and making full use of unlabeled data through two training stages to alleviate overfitting. Meanwhile, we propose a feature difference-weighted spatial attention module (FDSAM) to highlight the subtle change areas and suppress background noise, thereby improving the positioning accuracy of small and low-contrast buildings. Experiments on three benchmark datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. At a labeling ratio of 5%, the method achieves $F1$ -scores of 87.93% on LEVIR-CD, 89.01% on WHU-CD, and 65.71% on S2Looking, showing competitive performance relative to state-of-the-art methods. The results also suggest that the method maintains reasonable cross-dataset generalization, model efficiency, and training cost, providing a balanced tradeoff among detection accuracy, robustness, and lightweight design under limited annotation conditions.
item.authors: Zhenxing Li;Wenzhuo Li;Hongjuan Zhang;Jin Liu;Kaimin Sun;

item.title: GCEMNet: Grouped Cascaded Enhanced Mamba Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification in Spectrally Similar Scenarios
item.description: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification remains challenging in spectrally similar scenarios, where different ground objects may share highly overlapping spectral signatures and comparable spatial structures. In such cases, weak discriminative cues are easily obscured by redundant spectral and spatial responses, leading to confusion between categories with similar material composition or spatial patterns. To address this problem, this article proposes a grouped cascaded enhanced Mamba network (GCEMNet) for HSI classification in spectrally similar scenarios. GCEMNet follows a progressive feature learning pipeline. Specifically, the channel–spatial attention fusion (CSAF) module preserves subtle discriminative cues by jointly exploiting channel statistics and spatial structural information; the grouped cascaded Mamba fusion (GCMF) module, built upon multiple enhanced Mamba (EM) units, captures complementary local and global dependencies through grouped learning and cascaded propagation; and the cross-feature separation Transformer (CFST) reduces the influence of redundant spectral and spatial responses through correlation-aware feature modeling and cross-feature interaction. Extensive experiments on two public mineral HSI datasets and one agricultural HSI dataset demonstrate that GCEMNet achieves superior classification accuracy with moderate model complexity. Module comparison, ablation studies, visualization results, and computational complexity analysis further verify the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed modules in spectrally similar scenarios and scenarios with class imbalance.
item.authors: Bingyi Liu;Haichen Wang;Bo Zhang;Yaxiong Chen;Weizhen Han;Zongqi Ge;Mengwei Li;

item.title: SGLDet: Spectral-Aware Global–Local Dynamic Modeling for Multispectral Aerial Object Detection
item.description: Multispectral aerial object detection (MAOD) aims to exploit spectral–spatial cues to address object detection challenges in complex aerial scenes. Existing methods mainly focus on spectral–spatial decoupling and object-aware spectral–spatial fusion to improve spectral utilization. However, two critical issues remain underexplored: 1) severe foreground–background imbalance caused by large scene coverage hinders reliable object recognition and 2) aerial objects exhibit substantial local variations in scale, orientation, and structure, which hinder accurate localization. To address these issues, we propose SGLDet, a spectral-aware global–local dynamic modeling framework for MAOD, which is motivated by the observation that object semantics are jointly determined by global spectral consistency and scene context, while precise localization requires dynamic feature modulation conditioned on the input spectral and spatial properties. To realize these properties, SGLDet consists of three coordinated components: a spectral-driven global dynamic modeling (SGDM) module that aggregates spectrally related features across the scene via similarity-guided sparse matching; a multiscale global context integration (MGCI) module that constructs a compact scene memory for scene-guided contextual reasoning; and a spectral-aware input-dependent calibration aggregation (SICA) module that performs expert-kernel aggregation with scene-guided spectral–spatial calibration to enable adaptive local feature modulation. Extensive experiments on MODA, HOD3K, and DroneVehicle demonstrate that SGLDet achieves superior performance with competitive computational cost.
item.authors: Peng Zhang;Shuaihao Han;Tingfa Xu;Jianan Li;

item.title: CRS-Det: Consistent Region Semantic Modeling for Remote Sensing Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
item.description: Remote sensing open-vocabulary object detection (RSOVD) aims to detect objects beyond the categories annotated during training. Although vision–language models (VLMs) have significantly advanced this task, existing approaches often suffer from region-level semantic instability, where region representations are highly sensitive to contextual variation and background interference, limiting generalization to novel categories. To address this issue, we propose CRS-Det, which introduces feature-level region semantic modeling to stabilize region representations rather than relying on image-level region discrimination. In particular, we propose multiview region semantic consistency (MRSC) to learn stable region representations by enforcing semantic consistency across multiple views. To reduce the influence of irrelevant background regions, we design region-selective aggregation (RSA), which learns activation-guided spatial weights to emphasize object-relevant visual responses and suppress irrelevant background features. In addition, we introduce prototype-guided semantic alignment (PGSA) to refine textual embeddings using learnable semantic prototypes, improving region–text alignment without introducing image-conditioned prompts. Experiments on four remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over the controlled baseline and competitive performance against representative open-vocabulary detectors, with particularly notable gains on novel categories.
item.authors: Ming Liu;Jing Li;Dong Ren;Hang Sun;

item.title: Large Vision Model-Guided Masked Low-Rank Approximation for Ground-Roll Attenuation
item.description: Ground roll is a common type of coherent noise in seismic records, and its attenuation remains challenging due to its substantial overlap with useful reflections in localized regions. Previous attenuation methods can be broadly classified into global and local categories according to whether ground-roll-contaminated regions are explicitly identified. Global methods, however, typically impose uniform attenuation on both contaminated and uncontaminated regions, which may result in signal leakage or distortion of reflections. By contrast, local methods restrict attenuation to contaminated regions and are therefore less prone to unnecessary modification of clean areas. However, their performance is often limited by manually designed or simplistic model-based mask estimation strategies. To address these limitations, we propose a large vision model-guided masked low-rank approximation (LVM-LRA) framework for ground-roll attenuation. Within this framework, a promptable LVM is first employed to identify ground-roll-dominant regions in seismic records through multimodal prompting and to generate accurate, fine-grained masks. The estimated masks are then incorporated into an LRA model for ground-roll attenuation. A global low-rank constraint is imposed on the reflection component to preserve event continuity, whereas a mask-guided local low-rank constraint is imposed on the ground-roll component so that its separation is confined to the masked regions. An iterative optimization algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is further developed to solve the resulting model efficiently. Experiments on synthetic and field datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more effective ground-roll attenuation and better suppresses signal leakage than the baseline methods.
item.authors: Jiacheng Liao;Feng Qian;Yongjian Guo;Ziyin Fan;

item.title: Rethinking Multilabel Remote Sensing Image Classification Under Dual-Distribution Instance-Dependent Noise
item.description: Multilabel scene classification (MLC) is a fundamental task in remote sensing (RS). However, its performance is often limited by noisy annotations, where subtractive noise occurs when inconspicuous targets are missed and additive noise arises when visually confusing categories are falsely added. To simulate such annotation errors, the recently proposed instance-dependent multilabel noise (IDMN) method introduces the first instance-dependent noise generation strategy for RS MLC, driven by the intuition that hard label instances are more susceptible to mislabeling. Specifically, it leverages a single probability distribution of present labels to derive thresholds for both subtractive and additive noise generation. This design determines additive noise by requiring absent-label occurrence probabilities to exceed an irrelevant present-label threshold, leaving its quantity difficult to control and overlooking potentially confusing absent labels. To address this limitation, we propose dual-distribution IDMN (DD-IDMN), which explicitly decouples the score distributions of present and absent labels for calibrated noise generation. Empirical analysis under DD-IDMN reveals that additive noise yields more severe performance degradation than subtractive noise. To combat this DD-IDMN challenge, we propose the prompt-guided activation interference rectification network (PAIR-Net). Through cross-modal attention with learnable text prompts, it learns more discriminative RS feature representations. Furthermore, we introduce an activation-aware dynamic filtering (ADF) module to identify unreliable present labels for suppressing the more destructive additive noise under DD-IDMN. Experiments on UCMerced, AID, and MLRSNet demonstrate that PAIR-Net consistently outperforms representative noise-robust multilabel methods under complex instance-dependent noise. Our code is available at https://github.com/BasilLeave/PAIR-Net
item.authors: Xinlei Zhang;Fan Liu;Chuanyi Zhang;Xiaoying Ji;Wenhui Wang;Wei Zhou;Jun Zhou;

item.title: SegTrans-Diff: A Segmented Spatiotemporal Transformer With Echo-Aware Diffusion Refinement for Long-Lead Radar Echo Extrapolation
item.description: Accurate long-lead radar echo extrapolation is important for severe convective weather warning, but existing models suffer from echo displacement, intensity decay, and spatial blurring, weakening high-intensity echo detection and hazard-warning effectiveness. These difficulties arise because location-critical mesoscale evolution and uncertain convective-scale details require different modeling mechanisms. Deterministic models provide more reliable echo positions but tend to produce over-smoothed forecasts, whereas generative models can recover sharper structures but may introduce positional uncertainty or spurious echoes when weakly constrained by historical echo evolution. We propose SegTrans-Diff, a framework that decomposes 0–3-h extrapolation into segmented deterministic forecasting and echo-aware diffusion refinement. SegTrans predicts echo segments under segmented temporal encoding (STE), transforming asymmetric short-input long-output forecasting into segment-wise subtasks. Its SegTrans-Block combines window-wise global attention (WWGA) and frequency-wise temporal modeling (FWTM) to capture mesoscale organization and long-horizon temporal evolution. Built upon this location-aware forecast, the diffusion branch refines convective-scale details rather than generating echoes independently. The SegTrans forecast provides echo coverage, motion path, and mesoscale morphology, while encoder-derived spatiotemporal context (STC) carries historical echo-evolution information into denoising. Echo-aware gated spectral feature refinement (EG-SFR) uses forecast-derived echo and boundary gates to guide spectral feature refinement during denoising. Experiments on Shanghai radar echo dataset show that SegTrans achieves the highest pixel-wise critical success index (CSI) and Heidke skill score (HSS) among the compared models, while SegTrans-Diff improves neighborhood-based strong-echo forecast skill. Compared with DiffCast, SegTrans-Diff reduces the Fréchet inception distance (FID) by 42.8%.
item.authors: Fangli Wu;Huantong Geng;Jinzhong Min;Zhanpeng Shi;Shaoqiang Ma;

item.title: ER-Net: Evolutionary Refinement Architecture With Spectral Purification for Infrared Small Target Detection
item.description: Infrared small target detection (ISTD) remains challenging because extremely weak target signals are often submerged in strong, nonstationary background clutter. Although deep-learning methods have advanced considerably, many architectures exhibit approximately isotropic low-pass behavior, causing irreversible attenuation of the high-frequency details of dim targets in deep layers. This article proposes an evolutionary refinement network (ER-Net), a detection framework that mitigates information dissipation through recursive feature refinement. Its central contribution is an asymmetric enhancement path: instead of using a conventional symmetric architecture, ER-Net treats the raw infrared (IR) image as an independent reference stream that bypasses shallow sampling and enters the deep hub directly, thereby supplying prior guidance at the most information-sensitive levels. First, a spectral purification module (SPM) performs adaptive feature cleaning in the frequency domain to suppress background noise while enhancing target-salient responses. Second, an evolutionary refinement hub (ER-Hub) uses global statistical fingerprints of the raw image to control feature evolution dynamically. The hub combines an Evolutionary Refinement Unit (ERU), which progressively strengthens and concentrates weak-target responses through recursive refinement, with residual synergistic fusion (RSF), which corrects residual errors and compensates for signal loss in nonlinear mappings. Extensive experiments on Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics (NUAA)-single-frame infrared small target (SIRST), National University of Defense Technology (NUDT)-SIRST, and infrared small target detection (IRSTD)-1K show that ER-Net achieves a competitive overall balance in pixel-level localization and background suppression. With a lightweight parameter count and high desktop inference efficiency, ER-Net provides an architecture–performance trade-off suitable for efficient IR detection in complex scenes. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/LXJK123/ER-Net.git
item.authors: Sheng-Yu Dai;Jian-Hua Qin;Zhong Liu;Hong-Wang Zhao;Xue-Qin Zhao;Ting-Ting Huang;

item.title: GLRF: Underwater Image Enhancement via Global and Local Visual Reconstruction Fusion
item.description: Underwater images frequently suffer from severe quality degradation caused by complex environmental conditions and the scattering and absorption of light during transmission, which greatly restricts their utility in subsequent analysis and applications. To tackle this challenge, this article presents an underwater image enhancement method that converges global and local visual reconstruction fusion to improve image quality and accuracy of visual tasks, called GLRF. Specifically, we first implement global color correction using the attenuated channel compensation strategy and correct local color bias using the local overlap-weighted color compensation strategy. Subsequently, we propose a structure-constrained luminance reconstruction method with smooth brightness transitions and gradient constraints for global contrast enhancement, which reduces noise caused by uneven brightness and preserves image details, while traditional histogram-based methods may introduce noise and cause irreversible detail loss when adjusting the brightness distribution. Ultimately, we exploit wavelet decomposition and reconstruction to unsharp mask the low-frequency components and adaptively threshold denoise the high-frequency components to reconstruct a high-visibility result. The comprehensive experiments on four benchmark datasets have shown that our GLRF achieves competitive or superior performance on most evaluated metrics. Additionally, the results of our GLRF enhancement are beneficial for feature matching.
item.authors: Ling Zhou;Hengyu Li;Peixian Zhuang;Weidong Zhang;

item.title: AAFNet: An Asymmetric Feature Encoding and Active Energy Modulation Network for Multimodal Remote Sensing Forest Fire Detection
item.description: Forest fires pose severe ecological threats, yet dedicated multimodal architectures for such complex environments remain largely underexplored. Generic multimodal methods struggle to decouple heterogeneous physical properties, resist feature contamination during dynamic fusion, and preserve the fragile boundaries of microfires against deep semantic smoothing. To address these limitations, we propose an asymmetric feature encoding and active energy modulation network (AAFNet) for multimodal remote sensing forest fire detection. First, an asymmetric feature encoding is designed at the source. Within this architecture, the geometry-aware anchor (GAA) module is proposed to adaptively fit the nonrigid boundaries of smoke via decoupled deformable sampling. In parallel, the thermal-aware salient (TAS) module performs hierarchical wide-range perception operators to capture long-range thermal gradients and suppress radiation artifacts. Second, an energy-guided modulation (EGM) mechanism is formulated to dynamically allocate modality weights by quantifying instantaneous energy responses. This active regulation suppresses background interference and improves feature purity during fusion. Third, a decoupled difference reconstruction (DDR) unit is developed to explicitly reconstruct residual differences between adjacent feature hierarchies. This compensation maximizes the preservation of fine-grained textures for early stage fires. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of our approach. The proposed model achieves an mAP@50 of 75.2%, an mAP@50–95 of 52.1% on forest fire datasets with only 2.531 M parameters, which comprehensively outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both detection accuracy and deployment parameters. Moreover, cross-dataset evaluation further demonstrates the generalization capability of AAFNet under diverse environmental distributions.
item.authors: Qinwen Li;Haiyan Li;Fuhua Ge;Pengfei Yu;Guanbo Wang;Xiang Liu;Yitong Fu;Jinde Cao;

item.title: Bridging the Gap of Missing Modalities: Common-Specific Knowledge Learning Network for Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Classification
item.description: Multimodal learning has attracted significant attention in the field of remote sensing image classification due to its superior performance. Although multimodal data are often available during training, certain modalities may be unavailable during inference in real-world applications, posing a risk of performance degradation. To this end, we propose a novel common-specific knowledge learning network (CSKLNet) to bridge the gap of missing modalities. CSKLNet consists of two learning stages. First, complete multimodal knowledge is distilled from the teacher into the student under missing modalities, with the Wasserstein distance adopted to alleviate representation heterogeneity by minimizing feature distribution discrepancies. Second, two parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) adapters are inserted into the distilled student model to further exploit specific information from the available modalities. Compared with existing methods, CSKLNet not only inherits the common information from complete modalities but also fully leverages the available modality-specific information, thereby maintaining robust performance with missing modalities. Extensive experiments conducted on four distinct datasets indicate the advanced performance of the proposed method compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, with overall accuracy (OA) improvements of 1.34%–13.34%, 0.35%–3.54%, 0.55%–17.65%, and 0.17%–11.91% for hyperspectral image (HSI)–light detection and ranging (LiDAR) Houston2013, Trento, HSI–multispectral (MS) Houston2013, and QAI-Mangrove, respectively. The source code will be available at: https://github.com/ZhaohuiXue/CSKLNet
item.authors: Simin Zhu;Zhaohui Xue;Hao Wu;

item.title: Extracting Building Polygons With Attributes From Remote Sensing Images via Deformable Transformers
item.description: Vector-form building maps with rich functional and physical attributes benefit a range of applications including—logistics route optimization, disaster risk assessment, urban heat island analysis, housing price modeling, and more. However, most existing studies treat building polygon extraction and attribute prediction as separate tasks. In this work, we propose a unified Transformer-based network termed PolyAttNet, enabling the joint modeling of polygon geometry and associated attributes. First, PolyAttNet predicts densified building polygon vertices by smoothly deforming the initial vertices sampled on the bounding box toward real building boundaries, guided by ring-structured relative positional representations (RPRs). The explicit vertex deformation strategy outperforms previous Transformer-based methods, which lack structure-constrained vertex initialization. Then, a dual-branch vertex classification strategy that jointly exploits geometric and semantic features is introduced to remove redundant vertices, thereby constructing regularized polygon representations with reduced complexity. Finally, PolyAttNet develops a scalable attribute prediction module equipped with a query-dependent gating mechanism (QGM) to enable input- and task-driven context modulation and attribute extraction. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmark tasks demonstrate that PolyAttNet achieves state-of-the-art performance within a unified framework, outperforming task-specific expert models by achieving at least 2.7% higher AP for building polygon extraction, 10.4% higher $F1$ -score for joint polygon extraction and function prediction, and 15.3% lower mean absolute error (MAE) for joint polygon extraction and height estimation. Furthermore, the seamless adaptation of PolyAttNet to semantic-aware indoor floorplan extraction from density maps validates its cross-domain generalizability.
item.authors: Dawen Yu;Shunping Ji;Weiming Xu;Zhiyuan Zhao;Hao Cheng;

item.title: Wideband RFI Mitigation for Spaceborne SAR by Acquiring Prior Information via Time–Frequency Analysis
item.description: Operating in shared frequency bands, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) faces a complex electromagnetic environment, making radio frequency interference (RFI), particularly wideband interference (WBI), an increasingly prominent issue. WBI typically exhibits time-varying characteristics across pulses, with its amplitude and temporal location varying significantly. Despite these variations, WBI originating from the same source generally maintains stable intrinsic properties, such as bandwidth and duration, which can serve as useful prior information for WBI mitigation. However, due to the difficulty of WBI modeling, existing mitigation methods often bypass WBI parameter extraction, neglecting the utilization of prior information. Furthermore, these methods typically apply fixed filtering strategies across the entire WBI-containing pulse, ignoring variations in scattering intensity across different terrains. This leads to degraded mitigation performance in complex scenes. To address these issues, a WBI mitigation method that acquires prior information is proposed in this article. Specifically, through time–frequency analysis, WBI prior information is extracted from representative pulses identified via a spectral flatness indicator. WBI localization can be achieved by independently clustering strong- and weak-scattering regions, further optimized by the prior information. Finally, the eigen-subspace projection (ESP) method is applied to the localized time–frequency regions to mitigate WBI. Comprehensive experimental results on SAR data from diverse scenes confirm the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.
item.authors: Zijun Li;Zongsen Lv;Yanyang Liu;Ning Li;Lei Cui;

item.title: EFAWDet: Efficient Frequency-Role Assigned Wavelet-State-Space Fusion for RGB–Infrared Object Detection
item.description: Red, green, and blue (RGB)–infrared (IR) object detection leverages complementary visible texture and thermal cues to improve robustness under challenging conditions. However, existing feature-level fusion methods lack explicit frequency-role assignment: low-frequency semantic structures and high-frequency localization details are indiscriminately processed, squandering computation on redundant responses while suppressing the edge cues essential for precise localization. Moreover, global modeling operators such as Transformers and state-space models are uniformly applied to all frequency components, further degrading small-object boundaries. To address these issues, we propose a lightweight frequency-decoupled framework, namely efficient RGB-infrared detector (EFAWDet) that explicitly allocates distinct frequency bands to distinct detection functions. In EFAWDet, a multigroup wavelet fusion (MGWF) module decomposes dual-modal features and routes compact low-frequency components, which encode stable target-body semantics, to grouped cross-modal fusion. Then, a multigroup noncausal state-space duality (NC-SSD) performs noncausal global interaction confined within these reduced-resolution channel groups. Significantly, the separated RGB/IR high-frequency subbands are first adaptively fused through lightweight attention, then cached and reintroduced at the enhanced detection head (EDH) through inverse wavelet reconstruction as delayed localization compensation. This “low-frequency global modeling, high-frequency delayed compensation” strategy aligns the spectral properties of IR imagery with the frequency bias of state-space modeling, simultaneously reducing redundancy and preserving fine-grained localization cues. Extensive experiments on M3FD, LLVIP, forward-looking infrared (FLIR)-aligned, and DroneVehicle demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. EFAWDet-nano achieves 87.6% mAP50 and 58.7% mean average precision (mAP) on M3FD with only 2.5 M parameters and 16.5 GFLOPs (209.0 FPS), yielding a 99.1% reduction in parameter count compared to the YOLOv8-based FusionMamba while sacrificing merely 0.1 percentage point in mAP. The source code will be available at https://github.com/chenHeaven/EFAWDet
item.authors: Zhenghua Huang;Haiwen Chen;Qian Li;Yaozong Zhang;Chunhua Deng;Xin Xu;

item.title: SSAN: Structured Spatial Aggregation Network With Sparse Partition Routing for Cross-View Geo-Localization
item.description: Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) aims to retrieve images depicting the same geographic target across heterogeneous viewpoints. Drone–satellite matching remains challenging because holistic descriptors may dilute localized geographic cues, predefined partitions are sensitive to viewpoint- and altitude-induced spatial variations, and exhaustive cross-view interaction may introduce unreliable associations between spatially misaligned regions. To address these issues, we propose a structured spatial aggregation network (SSAN), which couples response-driven regional aggregation with training-time sparse structural regularization. In particular, the soft partitioning module (SPM) learns continuous partition-response maps directly from retrieval supervision and aggregates reduced visual features into structured regional descriptors. Area-aware normalization (AAN) further compensates for differences in partition-response area, attenuating excessive dependence of regional descriptor magnitudes on response extent. Based on the learned response layouts, sparse partition routing (SPR) constructs compact regional tokens, estimates bidirectional cross-view affinities, and retains Top- $r$ high-affinity associations for structural refinement. SPR is applied only during training as a structural regularizer, preserving independent query–gallery encoding at retrieval. Extensive experiments on University-1652, SUES-200, and multiweather University-1652 demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of SSAN under viewpoint, altitude, spatial-shift, and environmental variations.
item.authors: Fawei Ge;Xinao Wang;Leipo Liu;Huan Wang;Baofeng Ji;Pengju Si;

item.title: GOQFormer: Geometric-Offset-Guided Query Transformer for 3-D Plant Point Cloud Instance Segmentation
item.description: Accurate organ-level instance segmentation of single-plant point clouds is important for 3-D plant phenotyping and crop breeding. The majority of existing methods are based on offset-based clustering pipelines, which are susceptible to variations in clustering hyperparameters. On the contrary, query-based transformer frameworks reduce the reliance on explicit clustering, but still suffer from the lack of reliable structural priors for query initialization in plant point clouds. To address this limitation, we propose GOQFormer, a query-based 3-D instance segmentation framework guided by geometric offsets. GOQFormer learns voxelwise offsets toward instance centroids in the voxel grid and derives robust voxel weights from offset magnitudes. This enables instance-guided queries (ISQs) to be aggregated from high-confidence regions for improved initialization. During decoding, offset-refined positional encoding (ORPE) is incorporated into the multiscale query-based mask decoder to update query–voxel geometric references. GOQFormer integrates offset-based geometric priors with query-based mask prediction, thus eliminating the need for clustering-based postprocessing. Experiments on the five-species and eight-species benchmarks show that GOQFormer achieves the highest observed mean average precision (mAP) among the evaluated methods, with three-run mean mAP values of 0.9029 and 0.831, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of geometric-offset guidance for organ-level 3-D instance segmentation on the evaluated benchmarks and indicate its potential as a segmentation stage for subsequent plant-phenotyping analyses. The code and related resources are available at https://github.com/yangxin6/GOQFormer
item.authors: Xin Yang;Teng Miao;He Huang;Yan Wang;Tao Yang;Weiliang Wen;Xuemei Zhong;Tongyu Xu;

item.title: Multiscale Aerosol–Cloud Classification Algorithm of the DQ-1/ACDL
item.description: Spaceborne LiDAR is a unique tool for profiling clouds and aerosols globally. Following the retirement of the Cloud–Aerosol LiDAR and Infrared Pathfinder Satellite Observations (CALIPSO) mission, DQ-1, carrying the aerosol and carbon dioxide detection LiDAR (ACDL), now fills this observational gap. However, traditional single-profile aerosol–cloud classification algorithms often misclassify overlapping layers and generate “striping artifacts,” characterized by unrealistic horizontal discontinuities between adjacent profiles, which significantly degrade data quality and usability. To address these issues, we propose a multiscale classification algorithm that partitions LiDAR scenes using dynamic windows (ranging from $1\times 1$ to $8\times 8$ ) based on signal-to-noise ratio thresholds and classifies layers using particle backscatter coefficients rather than total attenuated backscatter (TAB). This approach effectively reduces striping artifacts and improves aerosol–cloud layer identification, achieving a 74.6% reduction in horizontal discontinuity compared with the cloud–aerosol LiDAR with orthogonal polarization (CALIOP) scene classification algorithm (SCA). Furthermore, comparisons with Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), CALIOP, and the Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2) for dust distribution, cloud-top height (CTH), and cloud phase show general consistency and physically reasonable behavior across diverse regions, supporting the applicability of the ACDL products. The proposed framework ensures the quality of ACDL datasets and offers a transferable approach for optimizing layer classification in other spaceborne LiDAR missions.
item.authors: Luhao Zuo;Feiyue Mao;Weiwei Xu;Lin Zang;Pengfei Hu;Xiuqing Hu;Jiqiao Liu;Wei Gong;

item.title: Physics-Informed Blind Deconvolution for Seismic Resolution Enhancement Based on Zero-Shot Learning
item.description: The limited seismic resolution significantly degrades thin beds identification and reservoir characterization. Conventional deconvolution methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, while supervised deep learning (DL) methods require extensive high-fidelity labels. Although some unsupervised methods reduce the dependence on labels, they often lack geophysical interpretability. In addition, most DL-based deconvolution methods assume a known wavelet, which limits their applicability in practical scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a physics-informed blind deconvolution workflow for seismic resolution enhancement based on zero-shot learning. Specifically, a three-stage progressive optimization strategy is proposed. An initial wavelet is first estimated by amplitude spectrum constraints and phase scanning. A dual-stream time–frequency network (DSTFNet) is then warmed up with the wavelet fixed to obtain a reliable initial reflectivity. Finally, the wavelet and the network parameters are alternately updated to achieve joint refinement of the wavelet and the reflectivity. In addition, we construct a joint loss function consisting of a physics-constrained Huber loss, and an L1 sparsity loss, which enhances physical interpretability and robustness to noise. Experiments on synthetic and field data demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits strong generalization and robustness.
item.authors: Wenshuo Yu;Shiqi Dong;Hongyuan Yang;Xintong Dong;

item.title: 3-D Spectral-Element Forward Modeling of Induced-Polarization Transient Electromagnetic Responses Based on the Caputo Fractional Derivative and Sum-of-Exponentials Acceleration
item.description: Induced polarization (IP) can produce slow late-time decay, negative transients, and polarity reversals in transient electromagnetic (TEM) data and therefore needs to be considered when interpreting sulfide mineralization, altered fracture zones, and other polarizable targets. This study develops a 3-D spectral-element formulation for grounded long-wire TEM electric-field responses in which the Cole–Cole conductive-polarization relation is expressed directly in the time domain using a Caputo fractional derivative. Nonuniform hexahedral spectral elements and high-order vector edge basis functions are used for spatial discretization. To avoid storing and repeatedly evaluating the complete fractional history, the weakly singular memory kernel is approximated by a sum of exponentials (SOEs), yielding recursively updated memory variables. The method is validated using a nonpolarizable layered Earth, a homogeneous polarizable half-space, a polarizable low-resistivity layer, and 3-D polarizable bodies. At comparable degrees of freedom, the third-order spectral-element method (SEM) produces lower errors than the first-order finite-element method (FEM). Under matched numerical conditions, the SOE scheme reduces explicitly allocated fractional-history storage from 7924.91 to 257.25 MB (96.75%) and total runtime by 12.85%–18.17% while preserving global response accuracy comparable to that of direct L1 convolution. Numerical experiments show that E ${}_{x}$ is sensitive to the Cole–Cole parameters, resistivity contrast, target position, and target configuration. A generalized Jiaodong geology-constrained model further demonstrates identifiable late-time responses from deeply buried, low-resistivity, highly polarizable bodies. The proposed formulation provides an efficient forward-modeling basis for the interpretation and future inversion of IP-affected TEM data.
item.authors: Xiaonan Zhang;Xiaoyue Cao;Liangjun Yan;Xin Huang;Xinyu Wang;Lei Zhou;

item.title: Efficient Least-Squares Extended Reverse-Time Migration Based on Local Cross Correlation Gradient Computation
item.description: Least-squares reverse-time migration (LSRTM) improves upon conventional reverse-time migration (RTM) by inverting for a reflectivity model that compensates for the Hessian blurring inherent in adjoint-based imaging. In data-domain LSRTM, however, each iteration requires cross correlation of the source and adjoint wavefields at identical time steps, necessitating either full wavefield storage or costly reconstruction—a bottleneck that grows prohibitive for large-scale imaging problems. When the migration velocity model is inaccurate, the problem is compounded by cycle skipping, which traps the inversion in local minima. To address both challenges, we propose a local cross correlation gradient computation (LCGC) within the least-squares extended RTM (LSERTM) framework. By restricting the cross correlation to a local time window around the excitation amplitude at each subsurface location, our method avoids source-wavefield reconstruction entirely: each iteration requires only one forward simulation and one adjoint migration. The subsurface-offset extension provides an additional degree of freedom that tolerates velocity errors of up to 10%. Memory demand is further reduced by applying Nyquist sampling to the stored local wavefields. We validate the least-squares extended reverse-time migration method based on LCGC (LCGC-LSERTM) on layered and modified Marmousi-2 synthetic datasets under both accurate and inaccurate velocity models. With a time window spanning two wavelet periods, LCGC-LSERTM achieves imaging quality indistinguishable from the conventional cross correlation method while reducing the source-wavefield storage requirement to as low as 0.32%. The method matches the noise robustness and wavelet-mismatch tolerance of the conventional approach and substantially outperforms excitation-amplitude gradient computation (EAGC). Our results demonstrate that high-quality extended LSRTM imaging is achievable at a fraction of conventional memory and computational cost, making it practical for routine subsurface characterization even when the velocity model is only approximately known.
item.authors: Weixin Yang;Bo Wang;Chongyang Han;Mingkun Zhang;Chi Fang;Wei Wu;Hui Zhou;

item.title: Multimodal Text-to-Set Remote Sensing Image Generation With Anchor Diffusion
item.description: Multimodal remote sensing imagery provides complementary information for Earth observation, yet acquiring large-scale, spatially aligned multimodal data is expensive and labor-intensive, motivating data-efficient multimodal image generation. Existing methods are primarily developed for single-modal synthesis or pairwise cross-modal generation and thus cannot explicitly model the scene structure shared by multiple modalities for multimodal set generation. This limitation makes it difficult to simultaneously preserve cross-modal spatial alignment and modality-specific fidelity. To address these issues, we propose anchor diffusion (AnchorDiff), a unified framework that is able to generate spatially aligned multimodal remote sensing images from textual descriptions. To enable text-to-set generation and multimodal spatial alignment, the proposed framework produces an optical image from the given text, which is then used to construct a modality-shared scene anchor as an explicit structural prior. Specifically, we devise a UNet-based AnchorMap extractor to learn a modality-shared anchor map from modality-specific patterns to constrain structural consistency across modalities. For the multimodal generative network, we implement a conditional diffusion with a structure–attention hybrid sampling (SA-Hybrid) strategy that integrates anchor-based structural control and reference-attention guidance, thus enhancing structural alignment while maintaining modality-specific fidelity. Experiments on benchmarks covering optical, multispectral, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), and digital elevation model (DEM) data show that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of both spatial alignment and modality-specific fidelity. Code will be available at https://github.com/kyh433/Anchor-Diff
item.authors: Yuhan Kang;Honghu Pan;Hao Liu;Qiang Liu;Weiying Xie;Leyuan Fang;Lorenzo Bruzzone;

item.title: Learning Orthogonal Layout Disentanglement for Fine-Structured Aerial Multiview Stereo
item.description: This article presents OLD-multiview stereo (MVS), a novel framework that learns orthogonal layout disentanglement for fine-structured aerial MVS (AMVS), which explicitly models the orthogonality among rooftops, vertical facades, and mutually perpendicular walls. Orthogonal layouts encode the fundamental structural primitives of urban scenes, yet severe perspective distortions in aerial imagery disrupt their geometric regularities, rendering latent learning of orthogonality unreliable in current methods. To disentangle the diverse orthogonal layouts, our OLD-MVS features three carefully crafted designs: a shared hierarchical encoder that progressively induces explicit orthogonal structure representations using vision foundation model (VFM) priors through end-to-end depth optimization, an asymmetric depth hypothesis that perceives depth variability and reveals distinct uncertainty characteristics across orthogonal layouts, and a bidirectional refinement pipeline that amplifies layout-aware features under global prior consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our OLD-MVS establishes a new benchmark on the WHU-MVS and WHU-OMVS datasets, notably achieving a 21.5% reduction in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) on WHU-MVS.
item.authors: Youkai Ke;Chenyu Zhao;Qiyuan Ma;Xianwei Zheng;Guisong Xia;Jianya Gong;

item.title: Lightweight Hyperspectral Domain Generalization via Sample-Specific Low-Rank Basis Mixture
item.description: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification often suffers from substantial cross-domain shifts arising from sensor heterogeneity, varying acquisition conditions, and scene-dependent spectral distortions—all of which significantly degrade model robustness in previously unseen environments. Moreover, most existing deep learning approaches rely on heavy architectures, hindering their deployment on resource-constrained platforms such as UAVs or onboard processors. To address these challenges, we propose the adaptive basis spectral network (ABSNet), a lightweight domain generalization (DG) framework that learns adaptive low-rank spectral bases for constructing sample-specific low-rank adapters. By integrating spectral–spatial representations through cost-efficient token modulation, ABSNet is designed to improve robustness to distribution shifts while retaining discriminative spectral information. In addition, the rank-constrained formulation retains representation capacity with minimal parameter overhead, making the framework suitable for edge-level deployment. Experiments on the Houston, Pavia, and HyRANK benchmarks show that ABSNet achieves accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods with only a small fraction of the parameters of the compared methods. Ablation studies assess the contribution of each component within the proposed framework. The code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/qiujialiang/ABSNet
item.authors: Jialiang Qiu;Mengqi Chai;Shuming Xiong;Qiang Zhou;

item.title: Bidirectional Entity Coupling Alignment for Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval
item.description: Due to the homogeneous backgrounds and cluttered layouts of remote sensing (RS) imagery, fine-grained local entities are indispensable for preventing cross-modal semantic mismatch. However, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods based on contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) encapsulate scenes into holistic global representations, diluting these critical local cues. To address this, we propose the bidirectional entity-level alignment network (BEAN), a unified fine-grained entity alignment paradigm. First, to avoid the semantic ambiguity of conventional extraction mechanisms, we introduce a symmetric visual and textual entity construction paradigm comprising a visual entity bank constructor (VEBC) and a noun-to-token index constructor (NTIC). Specifically, VEBC constructs a visual entity bank via layerwise extraction, while NTIC performs index-guided extraction of textual entity embeddings, jointly delivering semantically discriminative cross-modal entity pairs. Second, to counteract the submersion of local entities within global embeddings, we design the cross-modal entity-bidirectional adapter (CEBA). It drives bidirectional cross-attention between the global feature stream and localized entity tokens. This mutually enriches isolated entities with holistic scene context, while simultaneously reinjecting fine-grained entity cues back into the global representations, effectively reversing the dilution process. Third, to overcome the absence of explicit entity-level supervision in traditional global contrastive objectives, we propose the fine-grained entity contrastive loss, a sample-level formulation that provides direct supervision for explicit entity alignment without requiring manual positive–negative pair annotation. Experiments on RSITMD, RSICD, and UCM-Captions datasets demonstrate that BEAN achieves leading mR scores of 50.74%, 34.67%, and 60.56%, respectively, consistently outperforming both PEFT-based methods and the fully fine-tuned CLIP baseline across all three benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/JasonGravity/BEAN
item.authors: Mengru Ma;Jiaxu Guo;Wenping Ma;Licheng Jiao;Yuting Yang;Xu Liu;Lingling Li;Fang Liu;

item.title: SDMCNet: Spatial–Spectral Decoupled Mamba–MoE Collaborative Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Using the whole image as input for hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, the model needs to handle broader spatial dependencies and more diverse spectral variations. In modeling nonlocal spatial relationships, scanning based on fixed windows is prone to directional bias, leading to the loss of spatial boundary details. In addition, the high dimensionality of the data makes spectral distributions complex and spectral information redundant, thereby affecting the reliable identification and effective utilization of spectral bands. To address these challenges, we propose SDMCNet, a spatial–spectral decoupled Mamba–mixture-of-expert (MoE) collaborative network for image-level HSI classification. Taking the whole image as input, SDMCNet achieves a balance between spatial structure modeling and fine-grained spectral representation. Specifically, the spatial branch progressive spatial perception feature extraction (PSPFE) integrates local and global Mamba modules to capture short- and long-range spatial contextual dependencies. A boundary constrained enhancement module (BCEM) is further introduced to suppress oversmoothing and noisy perturbations near class boundaries, thereby preserving spatial boundary details. The spectral branch anchor routed expert spectral aggregation (ARESA) builds an anchor routed expert collaboration mechanism to adaptively select complementary spectral experts to model complex dependencies among spectral bands and obtain precise spectral band combinations. The two branches collaborate through spectral channel weighting, thereby achieving synergistic spatial–spectral modeling for image-level HSI classification. Extensive experiments on the Indian Pines (IP), Pavia University (PU), Houston 2013, and HanChuan (HC) datasets demonstrate that SDMCNet consistently outperforms representative methods, validating the effectiveness and potential value of using the whole image as input for HSI classification. The code is available at https://github.com/chai-xue/SDMCNet
item.authors: Xue Chai;Bingbing Lei;Wei Feng;Ruiqing Zhang;Zhipeng Liu;

item.title: Robust Marine CSEM Signal Enhancement in Low-SNR Environments Using a Mixed Multistable Stochastic Pooling Network
item.description: The marine controlled-source electromagnetic (MCSEM) method is used to reconstruct deep subsurface resistivity distributions. However, low-frequency ambient noise and instrumental interference reduce the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of observed responses and degrade the stability of resistivity inversion. To address this noise-induced inversion degradation under low-SNR conditions, this study proposes a signal enhancement framework that integrates a mixed multistable stochastic resonance (MMSR) model with an adaptive stochastic pooling network (SPN). The MMSR model enhances the target-frequency components of MCSEM responses while suppressing uncorrelated noise. Parallel stochastic resonance (SR) nodes are constructed for multichannel signal fusion, allowing the framework to accommodate complex noise patterns. A recursive least squares (RLSs) algorithm is then used to adaptively optimize the pooling weights for further signal enhancement. Synthetic results show that the multistable SR–stochastic pooling network (MMSR-SPN) method improves the average SNR by 13.79 dB and maintains consistent enhancement performance under varying noise levels. Field datasets further validate its practical applicability. The processed time-series waveforms exhibit more pronounced attenuation and periodic features, attaining a spectrum improvement ratio (SIR) of 14.2. The magnitude-versus-offset (MVO) and phase-versus-offset (PVO) curves become smoother and more continuous, and the derived inversion results are consistent with known stratigraphic records. Numerical simulations and field-data experiments confirm that the proposed framework effectively alleviates noise-induced inversion instability, providing a robust signal enhancement solution for geophysical electromagnetic exploration.
item.authors: Yihan Tian;Wanyue Zhang;Fan Yang;Suyi Li;

item.title: Characterization of Instrument Spectral Response Function of the Ozone Monitor Suite–Nadir for Atmospheric Ozone Profile Retrieval
item.description: The ozone monitor suite–nadir (OMS–N) onboard the FengYun-3F satellite provides an ozone profile measurement with a nadir spatial resolution of approximately $7\times 7$ km for the UV2/VIS channels. Accurate characterization of the on-orbit instrument spectral response function (ISRF) is critical for reliable ozone ( $\mathrm{O}_{3}$ ) retrievals. Although the ISRF was characterized prelaunch, on-orbit thermal variations and changing observational conditions may alter its spectral response. Using the OMS–N observed solar spectra, this study parameterizes the on-orbit ISRF with Gaussian, super-Gaussian, and flat-top super-Gaussian functions. The ISRF exhibits pronounced dependencies on wavelength and cross-track position. The full width at half maximum (FWHM) differs significantly between the central and edge fields of view, and the ozone fitting residuals at edge angles are consistently larger than those at nadir. These discrepancies are most evident in the ultraviolet (UV) band, where residuals exceed 2%, and the edge-to-center difference reaches up to 72.17%. Both the FWHM and the ozone fitting residuals demonstrate excellent temporal stability, with mean residual deviations below 0.17% and FWHM variations within 0.008 nm. Validation against ozonesonde observations shows that using the preflight ISRF introduces an O3 bias of 1.854 DU, while the super-Gaussian parameterization reduces the bias to 1.569 DU. Pandora observations show that the super-Gaussian parameterization provides a balanced performance among fitting stability, cross-track consistency, and retrieval performance among the tested analytical forms. Therefore, the super-Gaussian ISRF is suggested as a preferred parameterization for OMS–N ozone profile retrievals under the present validation conditions, while the preflight ISRF remains a strong reference baseline.
item.authors: Ge Mao;Chengxin Zhang;Xiaohan Wang;Ran Zhao;Shun Shu;Qian Wang;Yapeng Wang;Na Xu;Lin Chen;Cheng Liu;

item.title: How Many Independent Samples Does a Satellite Image Contain? Generalization Bounds for Spatially Dependent Data
item.description: Machine learning classifiers for remote sensing imagery are typically evaluated as though every pixel were an independent sample. Spatial autocorrelation violates this assumption, since neighboring pixels carry redundant information which inflates sample sizes. How many independent samples does a satellite image actually contain? For an $n \times n$ image whose spatial correlation persists over a range of $r$ pixels, the effective sample size is $\Theta (n^{2}/r^{2})$ , not $n^{2}$ . We prove this as a finite-sample upper bound for classifiers on spatially correlated data, and show via a matching lower bound that the rate is tight, and no algorithm can do better. We extend the results to images with directional correlation and spatially varying correlation structure. Our result justifies spatial cross-validation since block holdout with separation proportional to the correlation range achieves optimal generalization guarantees, while random holdout can underestimate confidence interval widths by a factor proportional to $r$ . We validate the theory on synthetic data and satellite image tiles from three sensors (Landsat 8, Sentinel-2, and Sentinel-1).
item.authors: Robin Young;

item.title: Reliability-Aware Spatiotemporal Consistency Regulation for Satellite Video Tracking
item.description: The satellite video single object tracking (SVSOT) remains challenging because low image quality and cluttered backgrounds yield unreliable target evidence. Although recent trackers have improved robustness by enhancing feature representations and cross-frame interactions, they lack regulation of the reliability of evidence used for recursive feature updates. As single object tracking (SOT) can be seen as a recursive process, once unreliable evidence is absorbed into the target state, it may bias subsequent associations, accumulate spatiotemporal inconsistency, and eventually cause tracking drift or failure. To tackle these issues, we propose SCRTrack, a spatiotemporal consistency regulation framework that regulates the formation of target evidence and its propagation and maintenance across frames. Specifically, a multilayer feature formation (MFF) module is proposed to inject shallow structural details into deep semantic representations, enhancing spatial discriminability while suppressing clutter-induced interference. A reliability-guided context propagation (RCP) module is further designed to estimate interframe correspondence reliability and uses it to modulate temporal state updates, reducing the impact of ambiguous associations on state evolution. In addition, a motion consistency preservation (MCP) mechanism is introduced to monitor motion-consistent response displacements under occlusion and similar-object interference, maintaining target identity when appearance-based evidence becomes unreliable. Extensive experiments on SatSOT, SV248S, and OOTB demonstrate that SCRTrack achieves the state-of-the-art performance and exhibits strong robustness across challenging satellite tracking scenarios.
item.authors: Xiaowen Zhang;Haijiang Sun;Hanqing Sun;Hongliang Chang;Xilai Wei;Chao Ma;

item.title: CASE: Frequency-Domain Consistent Remote Sensing Image Synthesis With Context-Aware Dynamic Semantic Fusion
item.description: Recent advances in large-scale pretrained text-to-image models have substantially enhanced semantic image synthesis. Nevertheless, generating high-fidelity remote sensing images (RSIs) remains challenging, particularly in preserving structural integrity and achieving precise semantic consistency across multiscale structures and complex scene contexts. In this article, we propose the Context-Aware dynamic SEmantic (CASE) fusion module, a novel framework for RSI synthesis that effectively unlocks the generative potential of pretrained models to address these challenges. Specifically, we construct a context-aware semantic map (CSM) to explicitly encode spatial layouts together with contextual information. Subsequently, a dynamic residual semantic fusion mechanism is formulated to adaptively integrate layout-level, contextual, and global textual semantics, enabling the synthesis of RSIs with coherent structures and realistic fine-grained details. In addition, a frequency constraint (FC) loss is proposed to regularize the frequency-domain characteristics of the synthesized images, further enhancing structural fidelity across scales. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CASE consistently improves structural integrity, semantic fidelity, and visual realism of synthesized RSIs. Moreover, when applied to data augmentation for downstream segmentation tasks, our method improves downstream segmentation performance under the evaluated augmentation protocol, boosting semantic segmentation performance by +2.89% d-mIoU on the challenging GID-15 benchmark.
item.authors: Junde Liu;Danpei Zhao;Bo Yuan;Wentao Li;Tian Li;Zhenwei Shi;

item.title: A 3-D Finite-Difference Method for Borehole Acoustic Field in Prestressed Porous Formations
item.description: Understanding how in situ stress affects acoustic wave propagation in fluid-saturated porous formations is important for stress evaluation in reservoirs by sonic logging. We developed a 3-D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method for borehole acoustic fields in prestressed porous formations. The model is based on the acoustoelastic theory of fluid-saturated porous media. We investigated the effects of uniaxial stress on monopole and dipole wavefields, and compared the acoustoelastic responses of dry and fluid-saturated formations. The simulations show that uniaxial stress changes the arrival times, attenuation, and dispersion characteristics of borehole waves. A crossover of flexural-wave dispersion curves under horizontal stress is observed, indicating stress-induced anisotropy. The waveforms and dispersion curves of flexural waves exhibit different responses to stress in dry and fluid-saturated formations. This suggests that fluid-solid coupling must be considered when using sonic logging to estimate stress in fluid-saturated formations. These results provide insights into acoustic wave propagation in a borehole surrounded by a prestressed porous formation.
item.authors: Zhiqiang Zhao;Jinxia Liu;Zhiwen Cui;

item.title: Retrieving Specific Differential Phase for Dual-Frequency Dual-Polarization Doppler Cloud Radar
item.description: The specific differential phase ( $K_{\text {DP}}$ ) is an indispensable polarimetric radar variable for investigating the microphysical properties of precipitation. Utilizing the differential propagation phase ( $\Phi _{\text {DP}}$ ) identified by a Rayleigh plateau detection algorithm based on the differential reflectivity ( $Z_{\text {DR}}$ ) spectra, the reflectivity differential phase (ZPHI) approach is extended to retrieve $K_{\text {DP}}$ for a frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) dual-frequency (one is at 35 GHz and the other is at 95 GHz) dual-polarization Doppler cloud radar. Three constraints are imposed on the ZPHI approach, including a range-partitioning scheme based on the fluctuation characteristics of $\Phi _{\text {DP}}$ , a nonnegative constraint on the specific attenuation, and a convergence constraint to terminate the calculation. The $Z_{\text {DR}}$ and $\Phi _{\text {DP}}$ spectra during a stratiform precipitation event on February 3, 2021, and the raindrop size and distribution drop size and distribution (DSD) dataset collected by a disdrometer deployed in Cabauw, The Netherlands, are utilized to demonstrate its practical performance. The result shows that: 1) the ZPHI approach is effectively extended to retrieve $K_{\text {DP}}$ in dominant Mie scattering situations. Radar-retrieved $K_{\text {DP}}$ at both frequencies can be well derived with a high spatio-temporal resolution, and agree well with DSD-derived $K_{\text {DP}}$ across the precipitation event; 2) the combined use of $\delta _{\text {co}}$ , $V_{\text {R}}$ , and $K_{\text {DP}}$ can adequately describe the relevant microphysical characteristics for the stratiform precipitation event, which agrees well with the evolution of surface DSD-derived $D_{0}$ ; and 3) the impacts of short-duration DSD changes can be well captured by the fluctuated $K_{\text {DP}}$ and $\delta _{\text {co}}$ at both frequencies, and the drop shape ratio (DSR) changes explain the residual $K_{\text {DP}}$ deviations at Ka-band, as another potential response to DSD changes within radar range bins.
